guarantees.claim: When intg_err is deasserted, reg_steer is 0 if tl_i.a_address[AW-1:0] falls inside [4096:8191]; otherwise reg_steer is 1.
When intg_err is asserted, reg_steer is forced to 1 regardless of tl_i.a_address.

assumptions.claim: The address range [4096:8191] corresponds to a non-register region (e.g., HMAC window) in the system memory map.
assumptions.risk: If the range is incorrect, reg_steer will misroute accesses, directing window reads to register space or vice versa, causing data corruption or security violations.

assumptions.claim: AW parameter is set to the full TL-UL address width so that the inside comparison evaluates all address bits correctly.
assumptions.risk: If AW is too small, address truncation will cause misclassification and incorrect steering.

assumptions.claim: intg_err reflects a genuine integrity error and is not spuriously asserted.
assumptions.risk: Spurious assertion forces reg_steer=1, blocking window accesses, potentially causing denial-of-service or masking real errors.

uncertain_points.claim: Hardcoded address range [4096:8191] may not match the actual HMAC window base/size defined elsewhere.
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatch leads to incorrect steering, possibly accessing wrong registers or FIFO, causing functional failure or leaking secret data.

uncertain_points.claim: The use of reg_steer in downstream logic (e.g., read mux or FIFO access) is not defined in this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: If downstream interpretation is inconsistent, data could be routed to the wrong destination, causing read corruption or exposure.

uncertain_points.claim: intg_err is combinational; a transition mid-transaction could change reg_steer after the address phase, causing a mismatch in steering.
uncertain_points.cond: intg_err toggles during an active TL-UL transaction
uncertain_points.risk: The TL-UL interface may sample reg_steer at different times, leading to a partially steered transaction, data corruption, or protocol violation.
